context: Decide the single source of truth for FlightData query parameters and make both surfaces read it: either derive FLIGHTDATA_DEFAULT_PARAMS from the same data-coverage constants the SQL catalog uses (LAST_AVAILABLE_YEAR / the query catalog), or have the DataFrame runner call the existing set_parameter_overrides() with the SQL-side parameters. Do NOT special-case the gate -- the defect is in the product run path.
description: FlightData's two surfaces are parameterized from different sources. The SQL queries carry date literals derived from the data's actual coverage (get_query('best-routes') at SF=0.01 emits 2024-12-01 / 2025-01-01, from LAST_AVAILABLE_YEAR). The DataFrame surface instead uses a hardcoded FLIGHTDATA_DEFAULT_PARAMS = {start_date: date(2018,1,1), end_date: date(2019,1,1)} in benchbox/core/flightdata/dataframe_queries.py. The generator produces the LAST available year, so the DataFrame window matches ZERO rows: every FlightData DataFrame query returns an empty result while the SQL query returns rows. This is not a gate artifact -- it means FlightData DataFrame runs have been timing queries over an empty date range, so their results are meaningless. Evidence: with the CSV-header loader defect fixed (PR #1441) the type errors disappear and all 20 queries x 2 backends still diverge with the identical signature 'Row count mismatch. Original: N, Variant: 0'. A set_parameter_overrides() hook already exists in the module, which suggests the runner was meant to supply parameters and does not.

preserves.behavior: The SQL surface's parameters are unchanged; the DataFrame surface moves to match the data, not the reverse

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from benchbox.core.flightdata.benchmark import FlightDataBenchmark as B;import re;q=B(scale_factor=0.01).get_query('best-routes');from benchbox.core.flightdata.dataframe_queries import FLIGHTDATA_DEFAULT_PARAMS as P;ys=sorted(set(re.findall(r'(\d{4})-\d{2}-\d{2}',q)));sys.exit(0 if str(P['start_date'].year) in ys else 1)"
verifications.description: the DataFrame date window covers the generated data
verifications.expected: exit 0 once aligned; exits 1 on an unfixed tree where the DataFrame window is 2018 and the SQL window is 2024/2025
